message.content: In lions, one of the most striking examples of a dominant genetic trait is the presence of a mane in adult male lions. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion: a single copy of the dominant allele (often referred to as **M**) is sufficient to produce a mane, while the recessive allele (**m**) results in a maneless phenotype. Thus, if a male lion inherits at least one dominant allele from either parent, he will develop a mane. This dominant trait is responsible for the characteristic appearance of male lions and plays a role in social signaling and mate attraction.
